help.tips[1].en.text: Mass nouns (Kaffee, Wasser, Musik, Wetter), plurals without an article (Kinder, Leute, Freunde), after numbers (drei kleine Kinder), after viele / einige / wenige (viele nette Leute), in ads and headlines (Schöne Wohnung, ruhige Lage).

help.mistakes[0].whyEn: Before a noun the adjective always has an ending; here it shows the accusative.
help.mistakes[3].whyEn: Genitive masculine/neuter with no article: the noun already ends in -s, so the adjective takes -en.
help.hookEn: Menus, flat ads and headlines drop the article — so the adjective has to carry the ending all by itself.
help.introEn: The third table completes the system, and it is the one with the clearest logic: when there is no article at all, the adjective takes over the article's job entirely and wears the der/die/das ending itself. Nominative: starker Kaffee (der → -er), frische Milch (die → -e), frisches Brot (das → -es), nette Leute (die → -e). Accusative: starken Kaffee (den → -en), the rest unchanged. Dative: starkem Kaffee (dem → -em), frischer Milch (der → -er), kaltem Wasser (dem → -em), netten Leuten (den → -en, and the noun takes -n). Genitive m/n is the one exception — guten Weines, not gutes, because the noun's -s already marks the case. The Nullartikel appears with mass nouns (Kaffee, Milch, Wetter), plurals (Leute, Kinder), after numbers (zwei kleine Kinder) and in headlines and ads — so flat ads, menus and newspapers are full of it.
help.rememberEn[0]: No article: adjective = article ending (starker, frische, frisches, nette).
help.recallEn.known: From the two adjective-ending lessons: after der and after ein.
help.recallEn.today: With no article at all, the adjective takes the article's own ending.
sentences[0].whyEn: With no article the adjective takes the article's ending: accusative masculine → -en (like den): starken Kaffee.
sentences[1].whyEn: Neuter nominative with no article: the das-ending -es — Frisches Brot.
sentences[2].whyEn: mit → dative feminine: the der-ending -er — mit warmer Milch.
sentences[3].whyEn: bei → dative neuter: -em (like dem) — bei schönem Wetter.
sentences[4].whyEn: mit → dative masculine: -em — mit großem Balkon.
sentences[5].whyEn: mit → dative plural: -en — mit guten Freunden.
sentences[6].whyEn: Accusative neuter with no article: -es — kaltes Wasser.
sentences[7].whyEn: After viele the adjective stays parallel: viele nette Leute — both with -e.
sentences[8].whyEn: Accusative neuter, no article: -es — frisches Obst.
sentences[9].whyEn: Accusative feminine, no article: the die-ending -e — laute Musik.
sentences[10].whyEn: mit → dative neuter: -em — mit kaltem Wasser.
sentences[11].whyEn: After viele: the parallel -e — viele junge Menschen.
sentences[12].whyEn: von → dative feminine: -er — von guter Qualität.
sentences[13].whyEn: mit → dative plural: -en — mit herzlichen Grüßen, like the letter formula.
sentences[14].whyEn: trotz → genitive masculine: -en (the noun already carries the -s) — trotz starken Regens.
sentences[15].whyEn: mit → dative feminine: -er — mit moderner Küche.
sentences[16].whyEn: für → accusative neuter: -es — für gutes Essen.
sentences[17].whyEn: wegen → genitive masculine: -en, the noun carries the -s — wegen dichten Verkehrs.
